findings_addressed.oracle: Independent oracle: the bridge initialises _display_mode='hex8'; after set_display_mode('hex32_le') the value stored in self._display_mode must equal 'hex32_le' (verified by asserting get_display_mode() == 'hex32_le' AND != initial 'hex8'). The key structural fix is removing pytest.importorskip('intellicrack_hexcore') from the test module and providing a local bridge fixture that constructs HexEditorBridge() directly — set_display_mode/get_display_mode are pure-Python methods that require no Rust extension.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/bridges/hex_editor.py HexEditorDisplayMixin.set_display_mode, change 'self._display_mode = mode' to 'self._display_mode = "hex8"' — test_roundtrip_hex32_le asserts mode == 'hex32_le' which fails because get_display_mode() returns 'hex8'.

notes: Root anti-pattern N3 (skip-masks-failure): the module-level pytest.importorskip('intellicrack_hexcore') caused all 19 display-mode and 6 highlight-rule tests to be skipped entirely whenever the Rust extension is not built, even though every test exercises pure-Python code paths. Fix: (1) removed the importorskip guard from the test file, (2) added a local @pytest.fixture 'bridge' that constructs HexEditorBridge() and calls initialize() without depending on the hexcore-guarded conftest. Two additional tests were added: test_invalid_mode_raises_value_error (gates the ValueError branch) and test_mode_does_not_change_after_invalid_set (gates atomicity of validation-before-assignment). All 21 tests are now unconditional gates.
